app_help.text: Suggested weights come from the double-progression rule and her log. The logger shows a chip when it is time to go up. Never give a kg number.
Reps in reserve means stop with that many reps still left. Beginners usually stop with 2 to 3 left.
Swap from the exercise card in the logger, or ask Coach when kit is busy. Changes apply to today only until she saves a preference.
She can move a planned session in the Planner. Coach may propose a move. Never say it is already done.
A week counts if she does at least one session. Hitting her weekly target is a gold week.
Food is framed as fuel for training. No calorie targets or food logs.
Saved Coach preferences live in Profile, Coach preferences. She can remove them there.
Rest by role: main lifts 2 to 3 minutes, secondary about 90 seconds, accessories 60 to 90 seconds.

exercises.name: Goblet squat
setup: Pick one dumbbell and hold it vertically against your chest, cupping the top end with both hands.
Stand with feet just wider than hip-width, toes turned slightly out.
exercises.feel: Fronts of your thighs and your glutes.
form_cues: Sit down between your heels, keeping your chest tall.
Let your knees travel forward in line with your toes.
Push the floor away to stand up, squeezing your glutes at the top.
exercises.taken_tip: Dumbbells are rarely all taken. If your pair is in use, grab the next weight up or down and adjust your reps.

exercises.name: Dumbbell box squat
setup: Stand in front of a bench, feet hip to shoulder-width apart.
Hold a dumbbell at your chest, or one in each hand by your sides.
exercises.feel: Thighs and glutes.
form_cues: Sit back until you lightly touch the bench.
Don't relax onto it: keep your weight in your feet.
Stand up tall and squeeze your glutes.
exercises.taken_tip: Any bench or box at about knee height works. Use a low one if a bench is taken.

exercises.name: Box squat to a chair
setup: Stand in front of a chair, feet hip-width apart.
Arms out in front for balance.
exercises.feel: Thighs and glutes.
form_cues: Sit back slowly until you touch the chair.
Keep your chest up.
Stand up through your whole foot.
exercises.taken_tip: Any sturdy chair, sofa or step works.

exercises.name: Leg press
setup: Sit with your back and head against the pad.
Place feet shoulder-width on the middle of the platform.
Push the platform up, then release the safety handles at your sides.
exercises.feel: Thighs and glutes. Feet higher on the platform means more glutes.
form_cues: Lower the platform until your knees are around 90 degrees, or as low as is comfortable without your lower back lifting.
Push through your whole foot.
Stop just short of locking your knees at the top.
exercises.taken_tip: If it's busy, ask how many sets they have left. Gyms are used to people sharing.

exercises.name: Barbell back squat
setup: Set the bar on the hooks at about mid-chest height.
Set the safety bars just below the lowest point of your squat.
Step under, rest the bar on your upper back, lift it off and take two small steps back.
exercises.feel: Thighs, glutes and your whole body working together.
form_cues: Brace your stomach like you're about to be poked.
Sit down and slightly back, knees following your toes.
Drive up and keep your chest proud.
exercises.taken_tip: Racks get busy at peak times. The Smith machine is the closest swap and often quieter.

exercises.name: Smith machine squat
setup: Set the bar at shoulder height and the safety stops just below your lowest point.
Step under so the bar rests on your upper back, with feet slightly in front of the bar.
Twist the bar to unhook it.
exercises.feel: Thighs and glutes.
form_cues: Sit down between your heels.
Keep your back against an imaginary wall behind you.
Push up and twist the bar back onto the hooks when you finish.
exercises.taken_tip: If the Smith machine is taken, a goblet squat gives you a very similar workout.

exercises.name: Hack squat
setup: Stand on the platform with your back flat against the pad and shoulders under the pads.
Feet shoulder-width, middle of the platform.
Release the safety handles.
exercises.feel: Mostly the fronts of your thighs.
form_cues: Lower slowly until your thighs are about parallel to the platform.
Keep your back flat against the pad.
Drive back up without locking your knees.
exercises.taken_tip: Not every gym has one. The leg press is the closest swap.

exercises.name: Leg extension
setup: Sit with your back against the pad.
Line your knee up with the machine's pivot point (usually a coloured dot).
Set the ankle pad just above your ankles.
exercises.feel: Fronts of your thighs.
form_cues: Straighten your legs smoothly.
Pause for a second at the top.
Lower slowly.
exercises.taken_tip: There isn't a close swap. Wait for it, or add a set to your squat or leg press instead.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift
setup: Hold a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs.
Stand hip-width apart with soft knees.
exercises.feel: Backs of your legs and your glutes. Not your lower back.
form_cues: Push your hips back like you're closing a door behind you.
Keep the dumbbells close to your legs and your back flat.
Stand up by squeezing your glutes.
exercises.taken_tip: Dumbbells are rarely all taken. If your pair is in use, grab the next weight up or down and adjust your reps.

exercises.name: Barbell Romanian deadlift
setup: Lift the bar from a rack or the floor so you're standing tall holding it at your thighs.
Hands just outside your legs, feet hip-width.
exercises.feel: Backs of your legs and glutes.
form_cues: Push your hips back and slide the bar down your thighs.
Lower until you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings, usually just below the knee.
Stand tall by driving your hips forward.
exercises.taken_tip: Use dumbbells or a fixed barbell from the rack if the barbells are busy.

exercises.name: Trap bar deadlift
setup: Step into the middle of the bar, feet hip-width.
Bend down and grip the handles in the centre.
exercises.feel: Glutes, thighs and backs of your legs.
form_cues: Chest up, back flat, arms long.
Push the floor away to stand up.
Lower with control by pushing your hips back first.
exercises.taken_tip: Most gyms have only one trap bar. A heavy kettlebell deadlift trains the same movement.

exercises.name: Kettlebell deadlift
setup: Stand with the kettlebell between your feet, in line with your ankles.
Feet hip to shoulder-width.
exercises.feel: Glutes and backs of your legs.
form_cues: Push your hips back and grip the handle with both hands.
Flat back, chest up.
Stand up tall and squeeze your glutes.
exercises.taken_tip: No kettlebells free? Hold one heavy dumbbell by the end in the same way.

exercises.name: Single-leg Romanian deadlift
setup: Hold a dumbbell in the hand opposite your standing leg.
Hold a bench or rack with your free hand for balance if you like.
exercises.feel: Back of the standing leg and its glute.
form_cues: Hinge forward as your back leg lifts behind you.
Keep your hips level, as if both hip bones are headlights pointing at the floor.
Return slowly to standing.
exercises.taken_tip: Dumbbells are rarely all taken. If your pair is in use, grab the next weight up or down and adjust your reps.

exercises.name: Cable pull-through
setup: Attach the rope to the lowest pulley.
Face away from the machine, holding the rope between your legs, and walk out a few steps.
exercises.feel: Glutes and backs of your legs.
form_cues: Push your hips back so the rope moves through your legs.
Keep your arms straight and relaxed.
Snap your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to stand.
exercises.taken_tip: If the cables are busy, a kettlebell deadlift or Romanian deadlift trains the same hinge.

exercises.name: Dumbbell glute bridge
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hip-width apart.
Rest a dumbbell across your hips and hold it in place.
exercises.feel: Glutes.
form_cues: Drive through your heels to lift your hips.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top for a second.
Lower slowly.
exercises.taken_tip: You only need a mat and a dumbbell, so you can do this anywhere.

exercises.name: Glute bridge
setup: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart.
Arms by your sides.
exercises.feel: Glutes.
form_cues: Push through your heels to lift your hips.
Squeeze at the top for a second.
Lower slowly.
exercises.taken_tip: Doable anywhere there's floor space.

exercises.name: Single-leg glute bridge
setup: Lie on your back with one foot flat and the other leg lifted or knee hugged in.
exercises.feel: Glute of the working leg.
form_cues: Push through the heel of the planted foot.
Keep your hips level as they lift.
Lower slowly.
exercises.taken_tip: Doable anywhere there's floor space.

exercises.name: Dumbbell hip thrust
setup: Sit on the floor with your upper back against the long side of a bench.
Rest a dumbbell on your hips and hold it there.
Feet flat, about hip-width apart.
exercises.feel: Glutes.
form_cues: Drive your hips up until your body is flat like a table top.
Chin tucked, eyes forward.
Squeeze your glutes for a second at the top.
exercises.taken_tip: No bench free? Do a dumbbell glute bridge on the floor instead.

exercises.name: Barbell hip thrust
setup: Sit with your upper back against a bench.
Roll a barbell over your legs to your hips and put a pad or folded mat under it.
Feet flat, about hip-width apart.
exercises.feel: Glutes.
form_cues: Drive your hips up until your body is flat.
Chin tucked, ribs down.
Squeeze for a second, then lower with control.
exercises.taken_tip: Benches near the barbells can be busy. A hip thrust machine or dumbbell hip thrust is the closest swap.

exercises.name: Hip thrust machine
setup: Sit with your upper back against the pad and the belt or pad across your hips.
Feet flat on the platform, about hip-width.
exercises.feel: Glutes.
form_cues: Drive your hips up until they're level.
Squeeze at the top.
Lower with control.
exercises.taken_tip: If it's taken or your gym doesn't have one, a dumbbell hip thrust works the same muscles.

exercises.name: Seated leg curl
setup: Sit with your back against the pad.
Line your knee up with the pivot point.
Lower the thigh pad onto your legs and put the ankle pad behind your lower calves.
exercises.feel: Backs of your thighs.
form_cues: Curl your heels down and back.
Pause briefly.
Return slowly.
exercises.taken_tip: The lying leg curl is the closest swap.

exercises.name: Lying leg curl
setup: Lie face down with your knees just off the end of the pad.
Ankle pad just above your heels.
Hold the handles.
exercises.feel: Backs of your thighs.
form_cues: Curl your heels towards your bottom.
Keep your hips pressed into the pad.
Lower slowly.
exercises.taken_tip: The seated leg curl is the closest swap.

exercises.name: Cable glute kickback
setup: Attach an ankle strap to the lowest pulley and wrap it around one ankle.
Face the machine and hold the frame, with a slight forward lean.
exercises.feel: Glute of the working leg.
form_cues: Kick your leg back and slightly out to the side.
Keep your hips square.
Return slowly.
exercises.taken_tip: If the cables are busy, a single-leg glute bridge works the same glute.

exercises.name: Hip abduction machine
setup: Sit with your back against the pad and the pads on the outside of your knees.
Set the start position so your legs begin together.
exercises.feel: Sides of your glutes.
form_cues: Push your knees apart.
Pause with your legs wide.
Return slowly.
exercises.taken_tip: Two similar swaps: cable hip abduction or side-lying hip abduction on a mat.

exercises.name: Cable hip abduction
setup: Attach an ankle strap to the lowest pulley and wrap it around the ankle furthest from the machine.
Stand side-on and hold the frame.
exercises.feel: Side of your glute.
form_cues: Lift your leg out to the side.
Keep your body upright, no leaning.
Return slowly.
exercises.taken_tip: Use the abduction machine or a side-lying hip abduction on a mat.

exercises.name: Side-lying hip abduction
setup: Lie on your side with your bottom knee bent for support.
Top leg straight, in line with your body.
exercises.feel: Side of your glute.
form_cues: Lift your top leg up and slightly back.
Keep your toes facing forward.
Lower slowly.
exercises.taken_tip: Doable anywhere there's floor space.

exercises.name: Dumbbell split squat
setup: Hold a dumbbell in each hand.
Take a big step forward so you're in a long stance, back heel lifted.
exercises.feel: Front thigh and glute.
form_cues: Lower your back knee straight down towards the floor.
Keep your front foot flat.
Push through your front foot to rise.
exercises.taken_tip: Dumbbells are rarely all taken. If your pair is in use, grab the next weight up or down and adjust your reps.

exercises.name: Bulgarian split squat
setup: Stand a big step in front of a bench, facing away.
Rest the top of your back foot on the bench.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand.
exercises.feel: Front thigh and glute.
form_cues: Lower straight down until your front thigh is about parallel to the floor.
Lean slightly forward for more glutes.
Push through your front foot to rise.
exercises.taken_tip: No bench free? A split squat with both feet on the floor is the closest swap.

exercises.name: Dumbbell reverse lunge
setup: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, or none to start.
exercises.feel: Front thigh and glute.
form_cues: Step one foot back and lower your back knee towards the floor.
Keep most of your weight in your front foot.
Push through your front foot to step back up.
exercises.taken_tip: Dumbbells are rarely all taken. If your pair is in use, grab the next weight up or down and adjust your reps.

exercises.name: Bodyweight reverse lunge
setup: Stand tall. Hold a wall or rail if you'd like support.
exercises.feel: Front thigh and glute.
form_cues: Step back and lower your back knee gently.
Weight in your front foot.
Push back up to standing.
exercises.taken_tip: Doable anywhere there's floor space.

exercises.name: Dumbbell walking lunge
setup: Hold a dumbbell in each hand.
Check you have a clear path of about 10 metres.
exercises.feel: Thighs and glutes.
form_cues: Take a long step forward and lower your back knee.
Push through your front foot to bring your back leg through into the next step.
Stay tall.
exercises.taken_tip: No clear space? Reverse lunges on the spot work the same muscles.

exercises.name: Dumbbell step-up
setup: Stand facing a bench or box, knee height or lower to start.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand.
exercises.feel: Glute and thigh of the leg on the box.
form_cues: Place your whole foot on the box.
Drive through that foot to stand up tall.
Step down slowly with the same leg.
exercises.taken_tip: Any stable bench or box at a comfortable height works.

exercises.name: Calf raise machine
setup: Stand or sit with the balls of your feet on the edge of the platform.
Shoulders or knees under the pads.
exercises.feel: Calves.
form_cues: Lower your heels slowly for a stretch.
Pause at the bottom.
Rise up as high as you can.
exercises.taken_tip: Dumbbell calf raises on a step are the closest swap.

exercises.name: Dumbbell calf raise
setup: Hold a dumbbell in one hand and a rail or wall with the other.
Balls of your feet on a step or plate.
exercises.feel: Calves.
form_cues: Lower your heels slowly.
Pause.
Rise up high.
exercises.taken_tip: Dumbbells are rarely all taken. If your pair is in use, grab the next weight up or down and adjust your reps.

exercises.name: Dumbbell bench press
setup: Sit on the end of a flat bench with the dumbbells on your thighs.
Lie back, bringing the dumbbells to your chest as you go.
Feet flat on the floor.
exercises.feel: Chest and the backs of your arms.
form_cues: Press the dumbbells up over your chest until your arms are straight.
Lower slowly until they're level with your chest, elbows at about 45 degrees to your body.
Keep your shoulder blades gently squeezed together.
exercises.taken_tip: No bench free? Do the same press lying on the floor, or use the chest press machine.

exercises.name: Dumbbell floor press
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand above your chest.
exercises.feel: Chest and the backs of your arms.
form_cues: Lower until your upper arms gently touch the floor.
Pause briefly.
Press back up.
exercises.taken_tip: You only need floor space and dumbbells, so you can do this almost anywhere.

exercises.name: Incline dumbbell press
setup: Set the bench to a low incline, about two notches up.
Sit back with a dumbbell on each thigh and kick them up to your shoulders as you lie back.
exercises.feel: Upper chest and the fronts of your shoulders.
form_cues: Press up and slightly towards each other.
Lower to the top of your chest.
Keep your feet planted and shoulder blades back.
exercises.taken_tip: If no adjustable bench is free, a flat dumbbell bench press is the closest swap.

exercises.name: Barbell bench press
setup: Lie on the bench with your eyes under the bar.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Set the safety arms just below your chest height, or ask someone to spot you.
exercises.feel: Chest and the backs of your arms.
form_cues: Lift the bar off and hold it over your shoulders.
Lower it to your lower chest with control.
Press back up, keeping your feet planted and shoulder blades squeezed.
exercises.taken_tip: Benches go fast on Mondays. Dumbbell bench press is the closest swap.

exercises.name: Chest press machine
setup: Adjust the seat so the handles line up with the middle of your chest.
Sit with your back flat against the pad and feet on the floor.
exercises.feel: Chest and the backs of your arms.
form_cues: Press the handles forward until your arms are almost straight.
Return slowly until you feel a light stretch across your chest.
Keep your back against the pad.
exercises.taken_tip: If it's busy, ask how many sets they have left. Gyms are used to people sharing.

exercises.name: Pec deck
setup: Set the seat so the handles are at chest height.
Set the arms so they start just behind your body.
exercises.feel: Chest.
form_cues: Bring the handles together in a wide hugging motion.
Keep a soft bend in your elbows.
Return slowly until you feel a stretch.
exercises.taken_tip: A dumbbell chest fly on a flat bench is the closest swap.

exercises.name: Dumbbell chest fly
setup: Lie on a flat bench with light dumbbells held above your chest, palms facing each other.
exercises.feel: Chest.
form_cues: Open your arms out wide with a soft bend in the elbows.
Lower until you feel a stretch across your chest.
Bring them back together in a hugging motion.
exercises.taken_tip: Dumbbells are rarely all taken. If your pair is in use, grab the next weight up or down and adjust your reps.

exercises.name: Incline push-up
setup: Place your hands on a bench, slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Walk your feet back until your body is in a straight line.
exercises.feel: Chest and the backs of your arms.
form_cues: Lower your chest to the bench.
Keep your body straight from head to heels.
Push back up.
exercises.taken_tip: Any sturdy surface works. The higher it is, the easier the push-up.

exercises.name: Push-up
setup: Hands on the floor slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Body in a straight line on your toes, or on your knees to make it easier.
exercises.feel: Chest and the backs of your arms.
form_cues: Lower your chest towards the floor.
Elbows at about 45 degrees to your body.
Push back up, keeping your body straight.
exercises.taken_tip: Doable anywhere there's floor space.

exercises.name: Seated dumbbell shoulder press
setup: Set the bench upright, or one notch back from upright.
Sit with your back against it and kick the dumbbells up to shoulder height.
exercises.feel: Shoulders and the backs of your arms.
form_cues: Press the dumbbells up until your arms are straight overhead.
Lower to about ear height.
Keep your back against the pad and ribs down.
exercises.taken_tip: No upright bench free? Do the same press standing, or use the shoulder press machine.

exercises.name: Standing dumbbell shoulder press
setup: Stand with feet hip-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height.
exercises.feel: Shoulders, with your core working to keep you steady.
form_cues: Brace your stomach and squeeze your glutes.
Press the dumbbells overhead.
Lower with control to shoulder height.
exercises.taken_tip: Dumbbells are rarely all taken. If your pair is in use, grab the next weight up or down and adjust your reps.

exercises.name: Shoulder press machine
setup: Adjust the seat so the handles start at about shoulder height.
Sit with your back against the pad.
exercises.feel: Shoulders and the backs of your arms.
form_cues: Press the handles up until your arms are almost straight.
Lower slowly.
Keep your back against the pad.
exercises.taken_tip: If it's busy, ask how many sets they have left. Gyms are used to people sharing.

exercises.name: Dumbbell lateral raise
setup: Stand tall with a light dumbbell in each hand by your sides.
exercises.feel: The sides of your shoulders.
form_cues: Raise your arms out to the sides until they're at shoulder height.
Lead with your elbows, with a slight bend.
Lower slowly.
exercises.taken_tip: Dumbbells are rarely all taken. If your pair is in use, grab the next weight up or down and adjust your reps.

exercises.name: Cable lateral raise
setup: Set a pulley to the lowest position with a single handle.
Stand side-on and hold the handle with the hand furthest from the machine.
exercises.feel: The side of your shoulder.
form_cues: Raise your arm out to the side up to shoulder height.
Lead with your elbow.
Lower slowly against the cable.
exercises.taken_tip: If the cables are busy, dumbbell lateral raises are the closest swap.

exercises.name: One-arm dumbbell row
setup: Place one hand and the same-side knee on a flat bench.
Hold a dumbbell in the other hand, arm hanging straight down.
Back flat, like a table top.
exercises.feel: Upper back and the side of your back.
form_cues: Pull the dumbbell up towards your hip.
Squeeze your shoulder blade back at the top.
Lower slowly until your arm is straight.
exercises.taken_tip: Rows are easy to swap: try a chest-supported row or the seated cable row.

exercises.name: Chest-supported dumbbell row
setup: Set a bench to a medium incline.
Lie face down on it with your chest on the pad and a dumbbell in each hand hanging down.
exercises.feel: Upper back, between your shoulder blades.
form_cues: Row both dumbbells up, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause at the top.
Lower slowly.
exercises.taken_tip: If no incline bench is free, do one-arm rows on a flat bench.

exercises.name: Bent-over dumbbell row
setup: Hold a dumbbell in each hand.
Hinge forward at the hips, soft knees and a flat back, until your upper body is at about 45 degrees.
exercises.feel: Upper back and the sides of your back.
form_cues: Row both dumbbells towards your lower ribs.
Keep your back flat throughout.
Lower slowly.
exercises.taken_tip: Dumbbells are rarely all taken. If your pair is in use, grab the next weight up or down and adjust your reps.

exercises.name: Barbell bent-over row
setup: Hold the bar with hands just wider than shoulder-width.
Hinge forward with soft knees and a flat back.
exercises.feel: Upper back and the sides of your back.
form_cues: Pull the bar to your lower ribs.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Lower under control.
exercises.taken_tip: If the barbells are busy, bent-over dumbbell rows are the closest swap.

exercises.name: Lat pulldown
setup: Set the thigh pads so they hold your legs snugly.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width and sit down.
exercises.feel: The sides of your back, under your armpits.
form_cues: Lean back very slightly and pull the bar to your upper chest.
Drive your elbows down towards your back pockets.
Let the bar rise slowly until your arms are straight.
exercises.taken_tip: If it's busy, ask how many sets they have left. Gyms are used to people sharing.

exercises.name: Assisted pull-up
setup: Choose the assistance weight. More weight means more help.
Step or kneel onto the pad and grip the handles.
exercises.feel: The sides of your back and your biceps.
form_cues: Pull your chest up towards the handles.
Lead with your elbows.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.
exercises.taken_tip: The lat pulldown trains the same muscles and is the closest swap.

exercises.name: Seated cable row
setup: Attach a close-grip handle.
Sit with your feet on the footplate and knees slightly bent.
Sit tall with your arms straight.
exercises.feel: Upper back, between your shoulder blades.
form_cues: Pull the handle to your belly button.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Let your arms straighten slowly without rounding forward.
exercises.taken_tip: If it's busy, ask how many sets they have left. Gyms are used to people sharing.

exercises.name: Single-arm cable row
setup: Set a pulley to about chest height with a single handle.
Stand or kneel facing the machine and hold the handle with one hand.
exercises.feel: The side of your back.
form_cues: Let your shoulder reach forward.
Pull the handle back towards your ribs.
Keep your hips and chest facing forward.
exercises.taken_tip: If the cables are busy, a one-arm dumbbell row trains the same muscles.

exercises.name: Face pull
setup: Set a pulley to about face height with a rope attachment.
Hold the ends of the rope with palms facing each other and step back.
exercises.feel: The backs of your shoulders and upper back.
form_cues: Pull the rope towards your eyes, separating your hands.
Finish with your elbows high and hands beside your ears.
Return slowly.
exercises.taken_tip: If the cables are busy, use the reverse pec deck or dumbbell reverse flys.

exercises.name: Dumbbell reverse fly
setup: Hold light dumbbells and hinge forward with a flat back, or lie chest-down on an incline bench.
exercises.feel: The backs of your shoulders.
form_cues: Raise your arms out to the sides with a soft bend in your elbows.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Lower slowly.
exercises.taken_tip: Dumbbells are rarely all taken. If your pair is in use, grab the next weight up or down and adjust your reps.

exercises.name: Reverse pec deck
setup: Sit facing the pad with your chest against it.
Set the handles so your arms start in front of you.
exercises.feel: The backs of your shoulders.
form_cues: Push the handles out and back in a wide arc.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Return slowly.
exercises.taken_tip: If it's busy, ask how many sets they have left. Gyms are used to people sharing.

exercises.name: Dumbbell biceps curl
setup: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
exercises.feel: The fronts of your upper arms.
form_cues: Curl the dumbbells up towards your shoulders.
Keep your elbows by your sides.
Lower slowly all the way down.
exercises.taken_tip: Dumbbells are rarely all taken. If your pair is in use, grab the next weight up or down and adjust your reps.

exercises.name: Hammer curl
setup: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your body.
exercises.feel: Fronts of your upper arms and your forearms.
form_cues: Curl the dumbbells up with your thumbs pointing up.
Keep your elbows by your sides.
Lower slowly.
exercises.taken_tip: Dumbbells are rarely all taken. If your pair is in use, grab the next weight up or down and adjust your reps.

exercises.name: Cable biceps curl
setup: Set a pulley to the lowest position with a straight bar or rope.
Stand facing the machine, holding the attachment with palms up.
exercises.feel: The fronts of your upper arms.
form_cues: Curl the handle up towards your chest.
Elbows stay by your sides.
Lower slowly.
exercises.taken_tip: If the cables are busy, dumbbell curls are the closest swap.

exercises.name: Triceps pushdown
setup: Set a pulley to the highest position with a rope or straight bar.
Stand facing the machine with your elbows tucked by your sides.
exercises.feel: The backs of your upper arms.
form_cues: Push the handle down until your arms are straight.
Keep your elbows pinned to your sides.
Let it rise slowly to about chest height.
exercises.taken_tip: If the cables are busy, overhead dumbbell extensions or kickbacks work the same muscle.

exercises.name: Overhead dumbbell triceps extension
setup: Sit on an upright bench holding one dumbbell with both hands above your head.
exercises.feel: The backs of your upper arms.
form_cues: Lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending your elbows.
Keep your elbows pointing up.
Straighten your arms to lift it back up.
exercises.taken_tip: Dumbbells are rarely all taken. If your pair is in use, grab the next weight up or down and adjust your reps.

exercises.name: Dumbbell triceps kickback
setup: Place one hand and knee on a bench, like a one-arm row.
Hold a light dumbbell with your upper arm tucked against your side.
exercises.feel: The back of your upper arm.
form_cues: Straighten your arm back behind you.
Keep your upper arm still.
Bend back to the start slowly.
exercises.taken_tip: Dumbbells are rarely all taken. If your pair is in use, grab the next weight up or down and adjust your reps.

exercises.name: Dead bug
setup: Lie on your back with your arms pointing to the ceiling.
Lift your knees so they're bent at 90 degrees over your hips.
exercises.feel: Deep in your stomach, around your belly button.
form_cues: Gently press your lower back into the mat and keep it there.
Slowly lower one arm behind you and the opposite leg towards the floor.
Return and switch sides.
exercises.taken_tip: Doable anywhere there's floor space.

exercises.name: Bird dog
setup: Kneel on all fours, hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
exercises.feel: Your core and the muscles along your back.
form_cues: Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are straight.
Keep your hips level, as if balancing a cup of tea on your back.
Return slowly and switch sides.
exercises.taken_tip: Doable anywhere there's floor space.

exercises.name: Side plank
setup: Lie on your side with your elbow under your shoulder.
Bend your knees to start, or straighten your legs to make it harder.
exercises.feel: The side of your waist.
form_cues: Lift your hips so your body is in a straight line.
Keep your hips stacked, not rolling forward or back.
Breathe steadily throughout.
exercises.taken_tip: Doable anywhere there's floor space.

exercises.name: Forearm plank
setup: Lie face down and prop yourself up on your forearms, elbows under your shoulders.
Start on your knees, or on your toes to make it harder.
exercises.feel: All around your middle.
form_cues: Lift your body into a straight line from head to heels.
Squeeze your glutes and gently pull your belly button in.
Keep breathing.
exercises.taken_tip: Doable anywhere there's floor space.

exercises.name: Pallof press
setup: Set a pulley to chest height with a single handle.
Stand side-on to the machine, hold the handle at your chest with both hands and step away until the cable is tight.
exercises.feel: The sides of your waist, working to stop you turning.
form_cues: Press the handle straight out in front of you.
Don't let the cable twist you towards the machine.
Bring it back to your chest slowly.
exercises.taken_tip: If the cables are busy, a side plank trains the same muscles.

exercises.name: Cable crunch
setup: Attach a rope to the highest pulley.
Kneel facing the machine and hold the rope beside your head.
exercises.feel: The front of your stomach.
form_cues: Curl your ribs down towards your hips.
Keep your hips still; don't sit back onto your heels.
Return slowly until your back is long.
exercises.taken_tip: If the cables are busy, reverse crunches on a mat work the same muscles.

exercises.name: Reverse crunch
setup: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet off the floor.
Arms by your sides, palms down.
exercises.feel: The lower part of your stomach.
form_cues: Curl your hips off the mat, bringing your knees towards your chest.
Lower slowly.
Use your stomach, not momentum.
exercises.taken_tip: Doable anywhere there's floor space.

exercises.name: Hanging knee raise
setup: Stand on the captain's chair with your forearms on the pads and back against the backrest.
Let your legs hang straight down.
exercises.feel: The front of your stomach.
form_cues: Lift your knees towards your chest.
Curl your hips up slightly at the top.
Lower slowly without swinging.
exercises.taken_tip: If the captain's chair is taken, reverse crunches on a mat work the same muscles.

exercises.name: Farmer carry
setup: Pick up a heavy dumbbell in each hand.
Stand tall with your shoulders back.
exercises.feel: Your grip, shoulders and whole middle.
form_cues: Walk slowly with short, steady steps.
Keep your shoulders level and your chest up.
Put the dumbbells down carefully at the end.
exercises.taken_tip: No space to walk? March slowly on the spot holding the dumbbells.

exercises.name: Suitcase carry
setup: Pick up one heavy dumbbell in one hand, like a suitcase.
exercises.feel: The side of your waist and your grip.
form_cues: Walk slowly and stay upright.
Don't lean towards or away from the weight.
Switch hands and repeat.
exercises.taken_tip: No space to walk? Hold the dumbbell and march slowly on the spot.

machines.name: Treadmill
aliases: Moving walking belt with side rails, a front console, and a clip-on safety key.
machines.visual_features: Moving walking belt with side rails, a front console, and a clip-on safety key.
machines.where: In the cardio area, usually in rows facing windows or screens.
setup: Clip the safety key to your clothing before you start. If you slip, it pulls out and the belt stops.
Stand on the side rails, not the belt, while you press Start or Quick Start.
start_and_stop: Press Start and let the belt begin slowly. Step on once it's moving at walking pace.
Change speed and incline with the arrows or quick-select buttons.
To stop, lower the speed first, then press Stop. Step onto the side rails once the belt slows right down.
In an emergency, pull the safety key or press the red stop button.
machines.beginner: Walking: 4 to 5.5 km/h. Incline: 0 to 6% to start. A 1% incline feels closest to walking outdoors.

machines.name: Exercise bike
aliases: Upright or recumbent cycle with pedals, a saddle, and a small console.
machines.visual_features: Upright or recumbent cycle with pedals, a saddle, and a small console.
machines.where: In the cardio area. Upright bikes look like a road bike; recumbent bikes have a seat with a backrest.
setup: Stand next to the bike and set the seat level with your hip bone.
Sit on and check: at the bottom of the pedal stroke, your knee should be slightly bent.
Slide your feet into the pedal straps so the ball of your foot is over the pedal.
start_and_stop: Most bikes start when you begin pedalling.
Use the plus and minus buttons to change resistance.
To finish, lower the resistance and pedal easily for a minute or two before getting off.
machines.beginner: Cadence: 70 to 85 rpm. Resistance: low enough to pedal smoothly, high enough that you're not spinning freely.

machines.name: Cross-trainer
aliases: Standing elliptical with two long moving handles and foot pedals on rails. Also called an elliptical.
machines.visual_features: Standing elliptical with two long moving handles and foot pedals on rails. Also called an elliptical.
machines.where: In the cardio area. Also called an elliptical.
setup: Hold the fixed handles and step onto the foot pedals one at a time.
Feet in the middle of the pedals, heels down.
start_and_stop: Start pedalling forwards and the screen will wake up.
Hold the moving handles to use your arms, or the fixed ones for balance.
To stop, slow down gradually. Wait until the pedals stop before stepping off.
machines.beginner: Resistance: low to moderate. Aim for a smooth, steady pace you could keep for 10 minutes or more.

machines.name: Rowing machine
aliases: Long rail with a sliding seat, a fan housing, and a pull handle on a chain or strap.
machines.visual_features: Long rail with a sliding seat, a fan housing, and a pull handle on a chain or strap.
machines.where: In the cardio or functional area, often on the floor near the walls.
setup: Sit on the seat and strap your feet in so the strap crosses the widest part of your foot.
Set the damper (the lever on the fan) to 3 to 5. Higher isn't better; it just feels heavier.
start_and_stop: The screen wakes up when you start rowing.
The stroke: push with your legs, lean back slightly, then pull the handle to your lower ribs. Return in reverse: arms, body, then legs.
To stop, row easily for a few strokes, then rest the handle in its holder.
machines.beginner: Damper 3 to 5. 20 to 24 strokes a minute. Smooth and long beats fast and short.

machines.name: Stair climber
aliases: Small moving staircase with two handrails and a console.
machines.visual_features: Small moving staircase with two handrails and a console.
machines.where: In the cardio area. It looks like a small moving staircase.
setup: Step onto the bottom stair while holding the rails.
Choose a low level before you start.
start_and_stop: Press Start and begin climbing as the stairs move.
Change speed with the plus and minus buttons.
To stop, press Stop and keep stepping until the stairs come to a halt. Step off carefully at the bottom.
machines.beginner: Start low (about 3 to 5 on most machines) for 5 to 10 minutes. It's harder than it looks.

machines.name: Leg press
aliases: Angled sled with a large footplate, a seat, and two safety handles.
machines.visual_features: Angled sled with a large footplate, a seat, and two safety handles.
machines.where: In the machine area, often near other leg machines. Look for a big angled sled with a seat and a footplate.
setup: Sit back with your back and head against the pad.
Feet hip-width on the middle of the footplate.
Add weight plates to the pegs on each side, or set the pin on a stack version.
machines.beginner: Start with just the sled or one small plate each side. Add plates evenly to both sides.

machines.name: Cable machine
aliases: Tall frame with one or two weight stacks, adjustable pulleys, and clip-on handles.
machines.visual_features: Tall frame with one or two weight stacks, adjustable pulleys, and clip-on handles.
machines.where: Usually a tall frame with one or two weight stacks and adjustable pulleys, in the machine or functional area.
setup: Slide the pulley up or down the column by pulling the pin and moving it to the height you need.
Clip on the handle you need (rope, single handle, bar or ankle strap). They're usually hanging on the frame.
Choose the weight by putting the pin in the stack.
machines.beginner: Start very light. Cable weights feel heavier than the number suggests, especially with one arm.

machines.name: Smith machine
aliases: Barbell fixed on vertical rails with hooks and safety stops, unlike a free squat rack.
machines.visual_features: Barbell fixed on vertical rails with hooks and safety stops, unlike a free squat rack.
machines.where: Looks like a squat rack with a barbell fixed on rails, usually near the free weights.
setup: Set the safety stops just below the lowest point you'll reach.
Position the bar at about shoulder height for squats.
Add plates evenly to each side if you need more than the bar.
machines.beginner: The bar alone usually weighs less than a normal barbell, often 6 to 15 kg. Check the label or ask staff.

machines.name: Squat rack
aliases: Tall free-standing frame with J-hooks and safety arms. The barbell is not fixed to rails.
machines.visual_features: Tall free-standing frame with J-hooks and safety arms. The barbell is not fixed to rails.
machines.where: In the free-weights area: a tall frame with hooks (J-hooks) and safety arms.
setup: Set the J-hooks so the bar sits at mid-chest height.
Set the safety arms just below the bottom of your squat.
An Olympic barbell weighs 20 kg; many gyms also have 15 kg bars. Use clips to hold the plates on.
machines.beginner: Start with the empty bar while you learn. There's no need to add plates until the movement feels steady.

machines.name: Lat pulldown
aliases: Seat with thigh pads and a long bar hanging from a high cable.
machines.visual_features: Seat with thigh pads and a long bar hanging from a high cable.
machines.where: In the machine area: a seat with knee pads and a long bar hanging from a cable above.
setup: Adjust the knee pad so your thighs are held snugly.
Choose the weight with the pin.
machines.beginner: Start light, around 15 to 25 kg, and focus on feeling your back work.

machines.name: Seated cable row
aliases: Low bench with footplates and a cable at foot height, often with a V-handle.
machines.visual_features: Low bench with footplates and a cable at foot height, often with a V-handle.
machines.where: Usually a low bench with footplates and a cable at foot height, near the lat pulldown.
setup: Sit with your feet on the footplates and knees slightly bent.
Clip on the handle you'd like (the V-handle is most common).
machines.beginner: Start light and keep your back still. Your arms and back do the work, not your hips.

machines.name: Chest press machine
aliases: Seated stack machine with two handles at chest height that press forward.
machines.visual_features: Seated stack machine with two handles at chest height that press forward.
machines.where: In the machine area, often near the shoulder press.
setup: Set the seat so the handles line up with the middle of your chest.
Choose the weight with the pin.
machines.beginner: Start at a weight you could press 15 times, then adjust.

machines.name: Shoulder press machine
aliases: Seated stack machine with two handles at shoulder height that press upward.
machines.visual_features: Seated stack machine with two handles at shoulder height that press upward.
machines.where: In the machine area, often next to the chest press.
setup: Set the seat so the handles start at about shoulder height.
Choose the weight with the pin.
machines.beginner: Start light: shoulders are smaller muscles than your legs and chest.

machines.name: Pec deck and rear delt machine
aliases: Seated machine with vertical pads or arms that meet in front of the chest; often reverses for rear delts.
machines.visual_features: Seated machine with vertical pads or arms that meet in front of the chest; often reverses for rear delts.
machines.where: In the machine area. The same machine usually does chest flyes (facing out) and rear delt flyes (facing the pad).
setup: For chest: sit facing away from the pad and set the handles so they start just behind your shoulders.
For rear delts: sit facing the pad and set the handles to the front position.
Adjust the seat so the handles are at shoulder height.
machines.beginner: Start light. These are small, isolation movements.

machines.name: Leg extension
aliases: Seat with a padded bar in front of the shins that lifts as you straighten your legs.
machines.visual_features: Seat with a padded bar in front of the shins that lifts as you straighten your legs.
machines.where: With the other leg machines: a seat with a padded bar in front of your shins.
setup: Line your knees up with the machine's pivot point (usually a coloured dot).
Set the pad so it rests on the front of your ankles.
Choose the weight with the pin.
machines.beginner: Start light and use a slow lowering. It's an easy machine to go heavier on than you need.

machines.name: Leg curl (seated or lying)
aliases: Seated or lying machine with a pad above the heels that you curl toward you.
machines.visual_features: Seated or lying machine with a pad above the heels that you curl toward you.
machines.where: With the other leg machines. Seated versions have a pad over your thighs; lying versions have you face down.
setup: Line your knees up with the pivot point.
Set the pad so it sits just above your heels.
For the seated version, lower the thigh pad so it holds your legs in place.
machines.beginner: Start light; your hamstrings may cramp if you go heavy too soon.

machines.name: Hip thrust machine
aliases: Back pad like a bench with a padded belt or bar across the hips.
machines.visual_features: Back pad like a bench with a padded belt or bar across the hips.
machines.where: In the machine or glute area, if your gym has one. It has a back pad and a padded belt or bar over your hips.
setup: Sit with your upper back on the pad and the belt or pad across your hips.
Feet flat, about hip-width, so your shins are vertical at the top.
machines.beginner: Start with a weight you can lift 12 times with a pause at the top.

machines.name: Hip abduction and adduction machine
aliases: Seated machine with pads on the outside or inside of the knees for outer or inner thighs.
machines.visual_features: Seated machine with pads on the outside or inside of the knees for outer or inner thighs.
machines.where: With the leg machines. Often the same machine does outer thighs (abduction) and inner thighs (adduction).
setup: Set the pads to the inside or outside of your knees, depending on which you're doing.
Choose a starting position that's comfortable.
machines.beginner: Light to moderate weight with a pause works best.

machines.name: Assisted pull-up machine
aliases: Tall frame with overhead handles and a knee pad or standing platform. More stack weight makes it easier.
machines.visual_features: Tall frame with overhead handles and a knee pad or standing platform. More stack weight makes it easier.
machines.where: In the machine area: a tall frame with handles at the top and a knee pad or platform.
setup: Choose the assistance with the pin. Here, more weight makes it easier.
Step up and kneel or stand on the platform.
machines.beginner: Start with plenty of assistance, often 30 to 50 kg, and reduce it over time.

machines.name: Hack squat
aliases: Angled sled with shoulder pads and a footplate. You squat under the pads.
machines.visual_features: Angled sled with shoulder pads and a footplate. You squat under the pads.
machines.where: In the leg machine area: an angled sled with shoulder pads.
setup: Stand on the footplate with your back against the pad and shoulders under the pads.
Feet hip-width, in the middle of the plate.
Release the safety handles.
machines.beginner: Start with the empty sled; it already has some weight.

machines.name: Calf raise machine
aliases: Standing or seated machine with a step edge for the balls of the feet and shoulder or knee pads.
machines.visual_features: Standing or seated machine with a step edge for the balls of the feet and shoulder or knee pads.
machines.where: With the leg machines. It may be standing or seated.
setup: Put the balls of your feet on the edge of the step, heels hanging off.
Set the shoulder or knee pads so they're snug.
machines.beginner: Moderate weight, a pause at the top and a slow stretch at the bottom.

articles.summary: A calm order of events for walking in, finding your spot and leaving with your first session logged.
articles.excerpt: Walking into a gym for the first time can feel like a lot. The good news: you don't need to know the whole gym. You need one session and a plan for getting through it. articles.summary: A simple kit list so you can walk in feeling prepared, without buying anything new.
articles.excerpt: You don't need special kit to start lifting. What matters is that you can move freely and feel comfortable. ## What to wear - **Something you can move in.** Leggings, joggers or shorts, and a top that doesn't ride up when you bend or lift your arms overhead. - **A supportive sports bra.** The most important bit of kit for many women. - **Flat, stable trainers.** For lifting, flatter soles feel steadier than thick, bo

articles.summary: What "3 x 8 to 12, 2 reps in reserve, rest 90 seconds" actually means, in plain English.
articles.excerpt: Your plan uses a few words that can look like code at first. Here's what they mean. ## Reps and sets - **A rep** is doing the movement once. One squat down and back up is one rep. - **A set** is a group of reps done back to back. articles.summary: There's no test to pass. Here's a simple way to find the right weight in your first set.
articles.excerpt: One of the most common first-session worries is "how heavy should I go?" The honest answer: lighter than you think, and you'll find your level within a session or two. ## The simple method 1. **Start light.** Pick a weight you're confident you can lift 12 times with good form. 2. **Do your first set** and notice how it feels. 3. **Adjust.** If you could easily have done 5 or more extra reps, go up a little for the ne

articles.title: Warm-ups and cool-downs: why they're worth five minutes
articles.summary: What each part of your warm-up and cool-down is doing, and why they're short on purpose.
articles.excerpt: Every Ascenda strength session starts with a short warm-up and ends with a short cool-down. They're quick on purpose, so you'll actually do them. ## What the warm-up does - **Raises your temperature.** A couple of minutes on the bike or cross-trainer gets your blood flowing. - **Moves your joints** through the ranges you're about to use, like squatting, hinging and reaching overhead. - **Wakes up key muscles**, like

articles.title: Gym etiquette: the unwritten rules
articles.summary: The handful of habits that make you look like you've been training for years.
articles.excerpt: Gym etiquette sounds intimidating, but it comes down to a few simple habits. Do these and you'll fit right in. ## The big five 1. **Put your weights back.** Return dumbbells to the rack and take plates off bars when you're done. 2. **Wipe down equipment.** Most gyms have spray and paper towels around. A quick wipe of the bench or handles after use is all it takes. 3. **Don't hog equipment at busy times.** Resting bet

articles.title: What to do when the machine you need is taken
articles.summary: Three calm options, so a busy gym never stalls your session.
articles.excerpt: It happens to everyone: you walk over to the leg press and someone's on it. Here's what to do. ## Option 1: Do something else first The easiest fix. Skip ahead to the next exercise in your session and come back. Most exercises don't need to be done in a strict order, apart from your main lift. ## Option 2: Use a swap Tap the swap button on the exercise. articles.title: How to share equipment (and ask "how many sets have you got left?")
articles.summary: Exactly what to say, what to expect, and why most people are happy to share.
articles.excerpt: Asking someone about a machine can feel awkward the first time. It shouldn't: it's one of the most normal things people say in a gym. ## What to say Wait until they finish a set (never mid-rep), then try one of these: - "Hi, how many sets have you got left?" - "Mind if I work in with you?" - "Are you using this bench?" articles.title: Feeling watched? Why most people aren't looking
articles.summary: The science behind why the gym feels like a stage, and why it really isn't one.
articles.excerpt: If you've ever felt like everyone in the gym is watching you, you're far from alone. In a 2025 Gymshark survey of 1,000 UK women, almost 9 in 10 said they'd experienced some form of anxiety in the gym. ## The spotlight effect Psychologists have a name for that feeling: the **spotlight effect**. We tend to overestimate how much other people notice us. In a well-known study, students were asked to walk into a room wear

articles.title: Your first time in the free-weights area
articles.summary: How the dumbbell and barbell area works, and how to make yourself at home in it.
articles.excerpt: The free-weights area is where the dumbbells, barbells, benches and racks live. It can feel like the busiest, loudest part of the gym. It's also where some of the most useful equipment is, and it's for everyone. ## How it's laid out - **The dumbbell rack**, usually along a mirrored wall, with pairs arranged from lightest to heaviest. - **Benches** you can move and adjust. Flat, incline and upright positions are set w

articles.title: How to brace your core when you lift
articles.summary: A simple way to feel stronger and steadier on almost every exercise.
articles.excerpt: "Brace your core" is one of the most common cues in the gym. Here's what it actually means. ## What bracing is Bracing means gently tightening the muscles all around your middle, front, sides and back, so your torso stays steady while you lift. It's not sucking your stomach in, and it's not holding your breath for ages. ## Try it now 1. Stand tall and breathe in through your nose, filling your stomach and sides. 2. I

articles.title: The hip hinge: the move behind deadlifts and hip thrusts
articles.summary: Learn this one movement and Romanian deadlifts, rows and kettlebell work all get easier.
articles.excerpt: The hip hinge is one of the most useful movements you'll learn. It's the pattern behind Romanian deadlifts, deadlifts, bent-over rows and cable pull-throughs, and it's how you should pick heavy things up in everyday life. ## What it is A hinge means bending forward by **pushing your hips back**, with only a small bend in your knees and a flat back. It's different from a squat, where your knees bend much more and you

articles.title: How to squat with confidence
articles.summary: Feet, knees, depth and the questions everyone asks about squatting.
articles.excerpt: Squats come in lots of versions: goblet squats, box squats, Smith machine squats and barbell squats. The basics are the same for all of them. ## Feet Stand about hip to shoulder-width apart, with your toes turned out a little. There's no single perfect stance. Find the one where you can squat down comfortably. ## Knees Let your knees travel forward and follow the direction of your toes. It's normal for them to go pas

articles.title: How to breathe while you lift
articles.summary: A simple breathing pattern for every rep, and when to keep it gentle.
articles.excerpt: Breathing is something people rarely think about until they're mid-set and realise they've stopped. ## The simple rule - **Breathe in** on the easier part, usually as you lower the weight. - **Breathe out** on the harder part, as you push or pull the weight. So for a squat: in on the way down, out on the way up. For a row: out as you pull, in as you lower. ## Bracing and breathing together On bigger lifts like squats

articles.title: Progressive overload, simply explained
articles.summary: The one idea behind every effective strength plan, and how Ascenda does it for you.
articles.excerpt: Progressive overload sounds technical. It just means **gradually asking your body to do a little more over time**. Your muscles adapt to what you ask of them, so to keep getting stronger, you need to keep nudging the challenge up. It's one of the core principles of strength training recommended by the American College of Sports Medicine. ## Ways to do a little more - **More reps** with the same weight. - **More weigh

articles.title: Reps in reserve: how hard should a set feel?
articles.summary: Why most of your sets stop before you're completely out of reps.
articles.excerpt: Your plan often says something like "2 reps in reserve". It's one of the simplest ways to make sure each set is hard enough to make you stronger, but not so hard that your form breaks down. ## What it means **Reps in reserve (RIR)** is how many more good reps you think you could have done when you finish a set. Researchers have developed scales based on this idea to help lifters judge their effort. - **3 reps in rese

articles.title: Why your routine has phases
articles.summary: Learn, build, test: why your plan changes every couple of weeks, and what each stage is for.
articles.excerpt: Every Ascenda routine is split into two or three phases, like "Weeks 1 to 2: learn the movements" or "Weeks 3 to 5: build". Here's why. ## Your body needs time to learn first In your first few weeks, a lot of your early strength gains come from your brain and muscles learning to work together. articles.title: Why sets, reps and rest change between exercises
articles.summary: Main lifts, accessories and core work each have a job. Here's how your plan sets them up.
articles.excerpt: You might notice that your first exercise of the day has fewer reps and longer rest than the ones that come after. That's on purpose. Each exercise in your plan has a **role**. ## Main lifts These are the big movements, like squats, Romanian deadlifts, hip thrusts and presses. articles.title: Sleep: your most underrated training tool
articles.summary: Why a good night's sleep helps you train better, and simple ways to get more of it.
articles.excerpt: Training is the signal to get stronger. Recovery, especially sleep, is when your body actually does the work of adapting. ## How much do you need? Most adults need around **7 to 9 hours** a night. Some people need a little more or less, but if you regularly wake up tired, you probably aren't getting enough. ## How poor sleep shows up in the gym - Weights feel heavier than usual - You lose focus or motivation more eas

articles.title: Sore after training? What's normal and what isn't
articles.summary: Muscle soreness explained, how to ease it, and the signs that mean you should stop.
articles.excerpt: Feeling achy a day or two after a session is very common, especially when you're new to training or you've tried a new exercise. ## Normal soreness This is often called **delayed onset muscle soreness**, or DOMS. articles.title: Rest days: why they count too
